title: What does your dream videogame concert look like?
text:
It feels like the last few years have seen a huge upsurge in videogame concerts, at least over here on British soil anyway. Undertale, The Legend of Zelda, Stardew Valley, The Witcher 3, Sonic, Metaphor: ReFantazio, Final Fantasy. The list goes on and on!
It's been a heartwarming sight—despite my saltiness at half of them happening in London, a city that is both too far away for a casual evening and also far too London for me to willingly set foot in it more than twice a year—but I still yearn to see more of my favourite songs in a live setting.
So it got me thinking, what would my ultimate videogame concert actually look like? Well, I'd probably be chucking in a whole lot of Square Enix nonsense a la Distant Worlds—give me Final Fantasy 10, FF12, FF14, and a little bit of FF13 on the side—but I would also kill to hear some Kingdom Hearts stuff with a live orchestra.
Then I'd probably take a pivot away from JRPGs entirely to hear some songs from my childhood. I continue to be utterly obsessed with the soundtrack from Rare's Kameo: Elements of Power 20 years after I first played it, and it's the kind of music that absolutely deserves the full orchestral treatment. And to wrap it all up? Chuck in a DJ set full of remixes from some classic Tekken games. Is that a major tonal shift? Yes, but it's my dream videogame concert, not yours. Get your own!
No, seriously, what would your dream concert look like? Is there a concert that already exists which you're desperately yearning to come to a city near you, or would you concoct some messed-up megamix even more cursed than my own? Leave a comment and be sure to let me know.

title: Kingdom Come: Deliverance studio co-founder says a lot of RPGs are 'still games for teenagers,' and that he's 'tired of all the RPGs where you are this chosen one'
text:
In a recent interview with PC Gamer's Joshua Wolens, Warhorse Studios co-founder Martin Klima traced the inspirations for Kingdom Come: Deliverance back to boredom with the typical RPG—kill the dark lord, romance a companion or two, and so on. Klima added that this formula is still a mite too widespread even now for his tastes, and wondered if gamers haven't outgrown it by now.
"I play a lot of RPGs, it's a genre I really like," he said. "I was really and I still am bored and tired of all the RPGs when you are this chosen one, when you have this grand task of saving the universe .. The games that are these really straightforward power fantasies. It's not that I think it's somehow wrong in principle. There is nothing bad about a good power fantasy. It's just, it's so repetitive."
He likened the typical fantasy roleplaying game to the old idler Progress Quest , a satire which lampooned EverQuest and its ilk for being time vampire-Skinner boxes. "It's really a distillation of what the common RPG is. So I found that there must be many, many people who are really tired of this formula and who want something new and different," he said. That formed the seedling which eventually germinated into KCD.
But things haven't changed much since then, in Klima's estimation. "The games that were and sort of are being made are still the games for teenagers," he said. "If you are 16, 17, you love playing these power fantasy games because it's something that you need. But the audience is much older today … everybody's going to think that I am hating on Expedition 33 right now, but that's definitely not the case."
As for why this sort of 'chosen one' story is still so prevalent, Klima reckons that publishers are primarily interested in trying things that have worked before. "They are really best at recycling the same formula over and over. When I'm talking about this, I really mean more games like games from Ubisoft, for example.
"I played the original Assassin's Creed, and the original Far Cry, and the original Watch Dogs, and most of these games in the first iterations, and it was fun. But once you play the same game for the 10th time, it sort of becomes stale." While Far Cry and Watch Dogs aren't exactly RPGs, it is notable that Assassin's Creed went through a whole era where it was doing its best Witcher 3 impression.
"Craftsmanship wise, [Ubisoft's] games are excellent. I mean, the beautiful animations, beautiful models. They are pretty much bug-free. It's a very polished experience," he said. "But I can't help but feel that this craftsmanship would be better served by creating a game that's a little bit more innovative." That said, he acknowledged the financial risks of experimenting with the sort of money Ubisoft throws around for all its flagship series: "I appreciate the dilemma that they have, and I don't have any easy answers for it."

title: It's easy to forget now, but the first Elder Scrolls game had a rough launch back in the day: 'It was a disaster in a lot of ways and somehow built a billion-dollar franchise'
text:
Given the legacy it created, it's easy to forget The Elder Scrolls wasn't a big deal right out of the gate. The original game in the series, The Elder Scrolls: Arena, wasn't badly received—our reviewer, Andy Butcher, gave it an 87 in his review at the time—but it didn't set the world on fire immediately.
In a retrospective on the making of Daggerfall over at Time Extension , Ted Peterson, designer on both the first two Elder Scrolls games, recalled the trouble Arena had moving copies when it first arrived on shelves in 1994.
"Game stores ordered a certain number of copies," he said, "and when we didn't ship on time, they started cancelling. To give you some context of how badly it did, the very, very first game I ever worked on was a retail pack for Terminator 2029, so you had to own the original game. That shipped more copies than Arena did early on. But we were lucky: word of mouth got out, and people started playing and enjoying the game. It was a disaster in a lot of ways and somehow built a billion-dollar franchise."
To help put that in context, Time Extension tracked down an interview Bethesda president Christopher Weaver gave in November of 1995 to some crusty old magazine called "PC Gamer" in which he was quoted as saying, "We were in unknown territory with Arena, and nobody seemed to believe that a company known for its sports games—no matter how good they were—could possibly break into a genre as insular, even fanatical, as RPGs. The word we were getting from buyers out in the field was: 'Hey, you guys can't do that!"
While Bethesda had released games in other genres, like the aforementioned FPS Terminator 2029, in the early 1990s Bethesda wasn't a name you looked to for RPGs. It was the studio responsible for Wayne Gretzky Hockey 3 and Gridiron!, which was why it was hired by Electronic Arts to help finish John Madden Football. (A relationship that ended in court when Bethesda sued EA for failing to publish a promised rerelease of Gridiron!)
Shifting Bethesda's reputation from "sports guys" to "RPG guys" took some doing, but Arena certainly managed it. I can only imagine the outcry today if Todd Howard announced we'd have to wait a bit longer for The Elder Scrolls 6 because the studio wants to finally get Wayne Gretzky Hockey 4 out the door first.

title: Warhammer: Blood Bowl is Blood Bowl 3.5 rather than a whole new game, but based on the beta it's definitely an upgrade
text:
It's a small thing, but being able to save and quit when I'm playing against the AI is a definite improvement in Warhammer: Blood Bowl. Though matches didn't take a huge amount of time in Blood Bowl 3, there were still nights where I'd find myself with 40 minutes before I should really go to bed thinking I can squeeze another game in, and then realizing too late I absolutely cannot.
A bigger change in Warhammer: Blood Bowl, though one that also makes it easier to squeeze in another match, is Rumble Mode. Based on the tabletop format called Sevens, it's a shrunk-down seven-a-side version of Blood Bowl played on a smaller pitch, inspired by 40K in 40 Minutes and Rugby Sevens. Each half has six turns instead of eight and rerolls cost twice as much, making failure much more common—and since a failed action results in a turnover in Blood Bowl, that speeds up play as well.
(Image credit: Slitherine) Rumble Mode isn't exactly the same as Sevens, though I'm playing the beta so details are subject to change. It doesn't have the Desperate Measures inducements, for instance, and you don't have to make one of your linemen a veteran (who is slower, but can reroll a few specific actions). But it still plays faster, and shakes up the tactics in interesting ways.
There's no line of scrimmage for a start. Instead of having to put three players on the frontline where they'll be biffing or being biffed from the outset, there's a no man's land between both teams. That means fragile teams aren't potentially down three players on turn one, which would be even more disastrous with only seven on the pitch.
The smaller pitch makes slow players less of a liability, and the expensiveness of rerolls means skills that let you reroll, like Dodge, get even better. My beloved Halfling team finally has a place to thrive, especially since their Halfling Master Chef can steal precious rerolls from opponents.
You can learn to play Rumble Mode easily since the first chapter of the campaign, carried over from Blood Bowl 3, now defaults to it. The three beginner games you play as default Ussingen Rookies have become seven-a-side, which makes the second match against Chaos Chosen a bit more challenging—getting the assists you need on those Strength 4 Chosen felt trickier to me.
From there you can opt to play the rest of the campaign in either Rumble Mode or as traditional matches, and Rumble Mode is also available in Eternal League, competitions, friendlies, and basically everywhere. It'll be interesting to see how popular it ends up being.
I don't know if I'm hallucinating, but the AI seems better at handling the reduced scope of these smaller matches. Improving the infamously dopey AI is an aim of Warhammer: Blood Bowl , and while I've only had a few days with this beta it does seem a little better. It still throws the occasional ill-advised block—the skink who took on a mummy must have been feeling real lucky that day—but at least it picks the best block die when it has a choice. I even saw it attempt a pass instead of defaulting to a cage around the ball carrier no matter which team it's playing.
I'll need more time with the playtest version to compare, but my first impression is that the AI is slightly less bad, even if it sometimes attempts a risky play before doing something safe like standing up a prone player. Which, admittedly, I'm guilty of in the heat of the moment too.
(Image credit: Slitherine) As well as Rumble Mode, Warhammer: Blood Bowl incorporates the tabletop game's third season rules update. I'm a big fan of the way it punishes stalling, with bored audience members throwing rocks at players who could score but elect not to, and rewards you with a bonus 10 grand at the end of a match if you don't stall.
The new Secure the Ball action lets you pick up the ball on a 2+ if you sacrifice the rest of that player's activation to do it, while the passing rules have been updated to get rid of Wildly Inaccurate results as well as deflections, both changes that encourage actually playing the ball instead of just lining up two teams and hitting each other until the bell rings.
(Image credit: Slitherine) The way Most Valuable Players are selected is different too—instead of a completely random player on your team earning bonus Star Player Points, only the six players you nominate (four in Rumble Mode) can potentially earn MVP. It means you're not punished for having spares on your bench by having them soak up Star Player Points you'd rather see go to someone more useful.
It's still the same Blood Bowl, but with some interesting tweaks. Changes that affect the balance or play out over the course of a tournament, like the Hatred trait players can gain after being injured, will take more time to judge, but I'm positive about the rules update so far.
(Image credit: Slitherine) Other positives in Warhammer: Blood Bowl are a landing page with tiles that can be personalized so you can leap right into whichever mode or ongoing competition you've put a pin in, and a player advancement screen that highlights which three skills other players tend to buy in this situation, with percentages for each. Is everyone else picking Guard for their mummies? Yeah, pretty much. It'll save me alt-tabbing out to see what the internet recommends when I'm playing a new team.
The beta doesn't include either of the new teams coming to Warhammer: Blood Bowl, so I haven't had a chance to try the Tomb Kings or Bretonnians. It also doesn't have the shop or season pass, so how that'll be implemented—and if there are changes to how teams are monetized—remains to be seen.
Warhammer: Blood Bowl's playtest will be available to the public from October 7 on Steam. The full release is scheduled to be out by the end of the year.

title: I got my start writing for a PlayStation 2 magazine: These are my 12 PS2-pilled recommendations from the Steam Autumn Sale
text:
What's great about the PS2 back catalogue is that it's too vast to have an encyclopedic knowledge of everything in there. The defining 20 or so games on the platform—God of War, Gran Turismo 3, Final Fantasy 10 and so forth—are very well known, and maybe Millennial players can recall a weirdo game or two like Mr Mosquito or Global Defence Force. One look at the games in the Japan-only Simple 2000 series, however, shows you just how deep the library goes. When's Demolition Girl getting a HD remaster, eh?
Still, we're in an era where it's not hard to rediscover the key games of that generation, partly because many platform highlights have found their way to Steam in various forms. Intriguingly, we've also reached a point where developers who grew up with this generation are designing great new games inspired by the classics.
Below you'll find six modern games that are inspired by what's known as the 'sixth generation' of consoles, plus six ports of Dreamcast/PS2/GameCube/Xbox-era favourites. I've kept the latter to games that didn't get a PC release at the time (so GTA: San Andreas would be ineligible, for example). All of the games in both lists are discounted in the Steam Autumn Sale .
PS2-inspired
Promise Mascot Agency
(Image credit: Kaizen Game Works) Promise Mascot Agency (40% off at $15/£13) is an open world game built around a novel management simulation layer. You send Japanese mascots off to various events while exploring an island that may or may not be cursed. It's actually one of the better open world games of recent years because every sidequest offers something meaningful, like additional mascots to manage or upgrades for your truck (culminating in flight capabilities, as pictured). It's also deeply PS2-pilled in its overall presentation, with its creators citing everything from Disaster Report to Persona 4 as its influences. "6 and 7 out of 10 PS2 games are what I live for," director Oli Clarke Smith told RPG Site . It shows in the marvellously unique finished product.
Hi-Fi Rush
(Image credit: Tango Gameworks) Hi-Fi Rush (55% off at £12.14/$13.49) is at the intersection of several great PS2-era phenomena: innovative rhythm action games, cel-shaded visuals and Devil May Cry-style 3D hack-and-slash combat. Tango Gameworks weaves in many other influences besides, including the way director Edgar Wright matches music to visuals in films like Shaun of the Dead and Baby Driver. It's not exactly at DMC or Bayonetta's level when it comes to hardcore combat credentials, but it's presented in an appealing and often breathtaking anime wrapping, and playing to the beat sets it apart. It captures the flavour of the PS2 era without being exactly like any single game.
Denshattack!
(Image credit: Undercoders) A leading candidate for my top 10 games of 2026, Denshattack! (25% off at $15/£12) draws inspiration from Tony Hawk's Pro Skater, but perhaps more crucially, blue skies Dreamcast classics like Crazy Taxi and Jet Set Radio. It's a speedrunning game of stunt jumping, grinding and rapidly boosting your train through regions of a corporate-owned version of Japan. Except the vision of it just keeps expanding, until you're eventually using said train to battle enormous robots and smash massive baseballs at bosses. Again, it's not exactly like any one of its inspirations—this is a special game because the developers draw something original from those sources.
Sifu
(Image credit: Sloclap) Capcom's God Hand is one of my favourite PS2 games. It was a true cult classic, riffing on Fist of the North Star with ludicrous cutscenes, but having one of the best third-person combat systems ever (and getting an infamous IGN 3/10 review for its trouble). There aren't many games that have been able to capture the physicality of its hand-to-hand brawls or customisable combos, but developer Sloclap has specifically called the game out as an influence on 2022's wonderfully brutal Sifu (75% off $10/£8). It's tonally a far more serious proposition, but its enthralling and beautifully animated fistfights did reawaken my God Hand muscle memory.
Kunitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess
(Image credit: Capcom) Outside of its well-known franchises, Capcom made a lot of random stuff for the PS2, like Chaos Legion, Auto Modellista, Gregory Horror Show and Clock Tower 3 (if you know what all of those games are, we are the same person). Kunitsu-Gami (25% off at £30/£25) feels like a lost stablemate to those: you recruit villagers to help you defend against hordes of demons that come at night, which are dead set on attacking the maiden you're charged with protecting. You also have a suite of hack-and-slash abilities to use, so it's an inventive hybrid of action and strategy. While there's no way it would've looked this handsome as a PS2 game, it's exactly the sort of thing you'd have expected from the publisher behind Killer7 and P.N.03. We gave it 86% .
Clair Obscur: Expedition 33
(Image credit: Sandfall Interactive) "Oh, these guys really like Final Fantasy 10," I thought when I first played Expedition 33 (20% off at $40/£34). To be fair, you feel it more in the world-building and story than the actual bones of its turn-based combat, which feel more like they're drawn from Lost Odyssey on Xbox 360 and Sekiro. The world-ending threat is so similar in Clair Obscur and FF10: the Paintress erases adults of a certain age on an endless cycle, and Final Fantasy 10's giant destructive whale Sin always comes back even if it's destroyed. The melancholy denizens trying to get on with life in a doomed but beautiful world is something crucial that the games have in common, too.
And now, some actual PS2 games
Metal Gear Solid 3: Snake Eater
(Image credit: Konami) A few years ago, you couldn't even play MGS3 on PC without an emulator—and now you have two decent ways to play it. The original version comes in the Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection Vol. 1 (50% off at $30/£25). Delta, the remake, is also 30% off. Take your pick, but I personally think the PS2 aesthetic holds up. MGS3 was the less hyped of the two PS2 Metal Gears, mostly because Sons of Liberty was used as an early tech showcase for the platform. But Snake Eater is a more complete game with superior boss battles and the best story in the series.
Final Fantasy 10/10-2 HD Remaster
(Image credit: Square Enix) RPG purists may argue Final Fantasy 12 is a better game—it certainly has stronger localisation and voice acting, and aims for mature storytelling over anime nonsense. It's the easy-to-parse combat and progression systems that keep me coming back to Final Fantasy 10 (60% off at $12/£8), not to mention how distinctive the world of Spira is. The soundtrack is loaded with bops, and might be the part of the game that's endured the most for me. If you like PS2-era Japanese RPGs, you're actually spoiled for choice on Steam: Phantom Brave, Tales of Symphonia, Grandia 2, Kingdom Hearts (if you don't mind stretching the definition) and more are also on sale.
Rez Infinite
(Image credit: Enhance) I always think of Rez as a Dreamcast-first game, but it was actually released simultaneously in Japan on both PS2 and Sega's final console. Still, it feels Sega to its core. This Panzer Dragoon-style rhythm shooter where you're fighting evil viruses in a computer network has a beautiful Y2K aesthetic, and Rez Infinite (70% off at $8/£6) brought it to modern platforms with a well-received expansion to the original game. It's not a long experience, so the price here is spot-on.
Shin Megami Tensei 3 Nocturne HD Remaster
(Image credit: Atlus) It goes without saying that Persona 3 Reload and Persona 4 Golden are easy recommendations from the Atlus RPG stable, since both games started their lives on PS2. Persona 4 Revival seems like it'll keep to the same standard , too. The publisher's other games were always a bit weirder and more impenetrable, though, like Nocturne (70% off at $15/£13), an atmospheric and hardcore monster battling game from the mainline Shin Megami Tensei series. Known as Lucifer's Call in the UK, it was my first exposure to Atlus. I never finished it and lost my save when my launch model PS3 died, but 20 years after I first played Nocturne, the specific dour feeling of its post-apocalyptic Tokyo still sticks in my memory. An acquired taste, but the people who love this game really love it.
Onimusha 2: Samurai's Destiny
(Image credit: Capcom) "I wonder what PC Gamer gave one of my favourite games of all time," I asked myself this morning. Turns out the answer was 65% . Oof! I love Onimusha 2: Samurai's Destiny (50% off at $15/£12.49), because it offers a branching path at numerous points in the story based on how friendly you are with the four different warrior companions in the game. Samurai's Destiny is at the midpoint between old school Resident Evil's fixed camera survival horror and Devil May Cry's hack-and-slash combat (except more methodical and less acrobatic). A great Steam Deck game, as you might expect.

title: Capcom's remake machine is ticking away, only problem is that means revisiting Resident Evil 5 and 6
text:
Amid celebrations for Resident Evil's 30th anniversary, executive producer Jun Takeuchi revealed what future plans Capcom had for the Resident Evil series, including what will happen after the devs run out of games to remake.
"The current 'Resident Evil' series is being developed along two tracks: the numbered titles allow players to experience the ongoing story of the series, while the remake series allows them to experience the past," Takeuchi says (via RENEWS ). This isn't new information as Capcom has begun its huge remake project in 2019 (with the Resident Evil 2 remake ) and has since gone on to give Resident Evil 3 and Resident Evil 4 facelifts as well, with the next scheduled to be Code: Veronica.
👀 Jun Takeuchi on the future of Resident Evil and the remake series eventually catching up with the numbered games."The current “Resident Evil” series is being developed along two tracks: the numbered titles allow players to experience the ongoing story of the series, while the remake series allows them to experience the past. Someday, the remake series will catch up with the era of the numbered titles, and we are already thinking about what we will do when that happens. In fact, we have been gradually preparing for that since around “Resident Evil Village.” The appearance of names such as Umbrella and Spencer, as well as the return of Raccoon City in “Requiem,” are also in preparation for a “crossover.”One of the reasons we regard “7” as a turning point for the series is that it was also the title where we began working on this kind of setup. At first, we included these elements with the sense that they were fan service, but users were far more delighted by them than we had imagined, and they even began analyzing the thoughts that the development team had privately kept to itself. So, as a series, we decided to respond to users’ expectations and pushed this setup further in “Village” and “Requiem.”(via: BIOHAZARD 30th Special Mook) September 30, 2026
It seems that Capcom is planning to finish remaking all the older games, perhaps pre Resident Evil 7 which Takeuchi deems as a "turning point" for the series. So if that's true we may expect to see the following:
Resident Evil 0: A yes from me, just to see Billy Coen again.
Resident Evil: Will this be the first remake of a remake?
Resident Evil: Revelations: This could go so hard in the hands of the RE remake team.
Resident Evil: Revelations 2: I'm in just so Moira could get a better backstory.
And then there are the big two, Resident Evil 5 and Resident Evil 6 ; it was bound to happen eventually. It was perhaps wishful thinking that Capcom was going to let these games slip into distant memory. While I think there is a world in which Resident Evil 5 and 6 could actually be redeemed, both games will need a hell of a lot of work and reshaping for this to happen, and I'd hate to see the series falter on these two games yet again.
(Image credit: Capcom) Let's just say Capcom does successfully remake all of these games and the world doesn't completely implode. All of these remakes will buy the studio about 12 years, with Capcom's current schedule of releasing a remake once every two years. Now, 12 years is a long time, but it's not forever, and I think Capcom intends to carry on forever. So what will happen when everything is remade? The cycle could just carry on with a Resident Evil 7 remake, it'd be about 21 years old at that point, or Capcom could have something else up its sleeve.
"Someday, the remake series will catch up with the era of the numbered titles, and we are already thinking about what we will do when that happens," Takeuchi adds. "In fact, we have been gradually preparing for that since around 'Resident Evil Village.' The appearance of names such as Umbrella and Spencer, as well as the return of Raccoon City in 'Requiem,' are also in preparation for a 'crossover'.
"One of the reasons we regard '7' as a turning point for the series is that it was also the title where we began working on this kind of setup. At first, we included these elements with the sense that they were fan service, but users were far more delighted by them than we had imagined, and they even began analyzing the thoughts that the development team had privately kept to itself. So, as a series, we decided to respond to users’ expectations and pushed this setup further in 'Village' and 'Requiem'."
While I appreciate getting to experience older games and get a hit of nostalgia, I'm far more interested in what Capcom has got on the drawing board for its new games. Requiem managed to free the series from the shackles of Umbrella (kinda, sort of, it was good enough for me). But I would love to see more twists, new plot threads, and new characters. The world of Resident Evil is far too interesting to get bogged down in remakes.

d1 决策模型如何工作

决策模型针对某个情境，为每个可能答案给出一个概率来回答问题。d1 决策模型接收非结构化数据（例如文本、图像或两者）以及一个或多个问题作为输入，在一次前向传播中读取它们，并返回概率，而不生成任何 token。一次文本决策耗时 200 到 300 毫秒，快到足以用于实时应用。

d1 回答三类问题：

Noul：一个是/否问题，用 0 到 1 之间的概率作答。
Choice：从多个标签中选一个，为每个标签给出一个概率。
Score：在一个量表上的位置，由每个等级的概率加权。

一个请求可以针对同一状态提出多个问题，从而节省输入 token。

d1 实战

当答案是结构化决策时，决策模型可以替代对语言模型的高成本调用。它们还催生了各种新用例，本节展示了其中一些。下面的每个演示都在 d1 Playground 中实时运行。

视觉检测。这个工业应用检查来自四条产线、经过摄像头下方的零件：电路板、蜡烛、腰果和口香糖（公开的 VisA 数据集）。d1 以 85-97% 的准确率分拣良品和缺陷品。最有趣的是，该模型从未为此训练过。得益于其出色的泛化能力，它能从一段简短描述中理解任务。

文本应用。五个应用将 d1 用于每一个决策：

Smart Filter：d1 成为 SQL 查询中的一个函数，WHERE d1(ticket, 'the customer wants to cancel)。它为 150 个支持工单逐一回答是或否。
Code Search：d1 逐层浏览 Hugging Face transformers 仓库（6,511 个文件），一次一个文件夹，直到找到能回答问题的那个函数。
Smart Folders：d1 将每个新文档归入一个文件夹，再归入一个子文件夹。它以同样方式归档搜索问题，因此关键词搜索只需查看一个子文件夹。
Web Agent：d1 根据一句话目标操作一个航班搜索网站。每一步，它都会在页面允许的所有操作中选出下一个动作。
Context Compaction：d1 读取编码智能体会话中的每个工具输出，并为下一个任务保留、裁剪或丢弃它。它移除了 52% 的 token，同时保留了任务所需的每一个输出。

我们改编了其中四个应用，来自以下开源项目： pg-jev、 jevgrep、 jev-ultrafast 和 fast-jev-compaction。

游戏。d1 实时玩八款经典游戏，并选择每一步。视觉在两方面帮助它：

更优的决策：俄罗斯方块完全可以用文字描述，但加入屏幕画面后，d1 的得分从消除 70 行提升到 81 行。
更简单的集成：在 Wordle 中，d1 直接从截图读取棋盘。开发者无需编写游戏的文字版本，而 d1 仍以平均 3.8 次猜测解决了 12 局中的 12 局。

d1 也能处理纯视觉任务。在 Quick, Draw! 中，它能在 62 个词中猜出玩家的涂鸦内容，并能识别 6 幅画中的 5.2 幅（随机猜测为 0.6）。

可用性与定价

立即使用 d1 决策模型开始构建，该模型已在 Liquid AI API 上以 d1 形式提供。在 console.liquid.ai 创建 API 密钥（Dashboard > API Keys）。

要使用视觉功能，您只需在 images 中以 base64 数据 URL 的形式发送图像：

代码
复制
import base64, os, requests

image = base64.b64encode(open("board.jpg", "rb").read()).decode()

response = requests.post(
    "https://api.liquid.ai/decisions/v1/systemone",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['LIQUID_API_KEY']}"},
    json={
        "model": "d1",
        "images": [f"data:image/jpeg;base64,{image}"],
        "state": "Camera image of a circuit board on the production line.",
        "questions": 
            {"defect": {
                "type": "noul", 
                "instructions": "Does this circuit board have a defect?"
             }
         },
    },
)

print(response.json()["answers"]["defect"]["noul"])

完整的 API 参考文档见 决策模型文档。

d1 仅按输入 token 计费，无输出 token。图像按与文本相同的费率计为输入 token：每 32×32 像素块 1.5 个 token，因此一张 1024×1024 的图像消耗 1,536 个 token。每个问题作为独立的提示计费，包括其文本和所有图像。

d1 也可通过 Vercel 和 OpenRouter 使用，目前仅支持文本。视觉功能即将登陆这两个平台。

这是 AI 创造与探索的激动人心的时刻，而 d1 仅仅是开始。我们正在继续开发各种规模的决策模型，带来新功能、更高的决策质量和更低的延迟，并计划很快在 Hugging Face 上发布即将推出的模型的开源权重。

Liquid AI，“Introducing d1: The most capable decision model, now with vision”，Liquid AI Blog，2026 年 10 月。

方法说明。我们于 2026 年 10 月 5 日使用 d1 Playground 的对比脚本对每个模型运行了每个应用一次。GPT-6.1 Sol 和 Claude Opus 5.5 将每个请求作为一条聊天消息接收并以 JSON 格式回答，采用其默认推理设置。当多个问题共享一个输入时，例如过滤器的工单或文件夹的段落，聊天模型会分批回答。成本使用标价，不含提示缓存折扣。d1 的成本使用每百万输入 token 0.04 美元。时间为每次运行的时间，最多 8 个请求并发。一次 Smart Filter 运行是对 150 个工单的一次查询。一次 Smart Folders 运行归档 105 个段落，其成本按每 1,000 个段落计算。过滤器的质量是其相对于人工标注的 F1 分数，该分数同时计入遗漏和错误的匹配。其他文本应用统计正确处理的目标、问题、段落或所需输出。我们在 d1 的流程设定后编写了 15 个代码问题中的 6 个以及 4 个压缩会话中的 2 个。在视觉检查中，每个模型都会看到来自同一产线的良品部件与待检查部件并排展示。

AI 导读

Together AI 发布 Together Link，把团队已用的编码智能体工具连接到 Together AI 上的开源模型，宣称可节省超过 50% 支出。

正文 · AI 翻译
中文
原文

概述

Together Link 将你团队已在使用的 harness 连接到 Together AI 上最好的开放模型，并将你的支出削减 50% 以上。同样的 agent，同样的工作流，账单却只是零头。

编码 agent 如今在工程团队中已司空见惯，而你交给它们的每一项任务，从一行修复到完整重写，往往都运行在同一个高端模型上。规模化之后，成本会迅速攀升：工程组织的支出从每月数万美元到数百万美元不等，全都花在闭源模型上。

开放模型已经大幅缩小了与闭源实验室顶级模型之间的差距。像 Kimi K3 和 GLM 5.3 这样的领先者，如今能以每 token 价格的一小部分处理许多最难的编码任务，而像 GLM 5.3 Flash 和 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 这样小巧而强大的模型则处理日常编码任务。Together Link 将它们带入你团队已经熟悉的工具中。

在你已经工作的地方工作

Together Link 支持 Claude Code、Claude Desktop、Codex（ChatGPT 应用和 CLI 中）、OpenCode 和 Pi。你的团队照常工作：设置和登录保持不变，没有新东西要学，而切回原生闭源模型只需一条命令。你只需几分钟就能在开放模型上跑起来。

快速开始
代码
复制
curl -fsSL https://link.together.ai/install | bash
运行一条命令即可设置 Together Link：你的 agent 会像以前一样打开，现在通过你的 Together AI API key 连接到 Together AI。创建一个账户以获取 API key。
使用“Auto”让 Together AI Router 挑选模型：它会读取每个会话的第一个任务，并将其发送到合适的模型：快速修复交给快速、低成本的模型，难题则获得前沿能力。如果你提供 Anthropic key，它会在 Opus 5.5 和 GLM 5.3 之间路由。如果不提供，它会在 GLM 5.3 和 GLM 5.3 Flash 之间路由。路由每个会话只发生一次，因此 prompt 缓存仍能正常工作。
查看每个会话后的节省情况。按会话跟踪器会显示你的实际支出，以及同一会话在 Opus 5.5 上本会花费多少。

计费使用你现有的 Together API key，按无服务器按量付费或积分包结算。你无需单独签约。

构建在开发者已经选择的无服务器平台上

Together Link 运行在 Together 的无服务器推理之上，这正是开发者已经在 OpenRouter 上为这些模型所选择的基础设施。Together AI 在 OpenRouter 上为 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash（40.8%）、GLM 5.3 Flash（28.2%）和 Kimi K3（23.1%）提供了最大份额的 token，整体速度和价格都极具竞争力。（截至 2026 年 9 月 30 日脚注）

Databricks Genie Phishing and Exfiltration

AI 导读

PromptArmor 报告称 Databricks Genie Code 执行上传的恶意 Skill 后，可在聊天渲染结果时弹出钓鱼页面并经用户浏览器外泄租户数据，全程无需人工批准。

正文 · AI 翻译
中文
原文
Databricks Genie 执行恶意 Skill，显示钓鱼模态框并在有控制措施的情况下外泄数据
背景

Databricks Genie Code 是 Databricks 中的代理式助手，使用户能够通过自然语言指令在其租户中操作数据。

Genie Code 可以在聊天中为用户渲染显示内容；恶意 Skill 可以利用此功能，在工具结果被查看时触发数据外泄，并向用户显示钓鱼攻击。

此攻击可在没有任何人工介入审批的情况下发生，也不受组织可能依赖的控制措施约束：

组织级 Skill 治理；Genie Code 从用户的个人工作区加载 Skill，而非从组织的受治理目录加载

在命令运行前对其进行评估的护栏代理；Databricks 将其视为尽力而为的生产力功能，而非安全控制

编码环境出口控制；出口流量来自用户的浏览器，而非编码环境

聊天中渲染的显示内容的沙箱隔离；显示内容随数据一起构建，无需访问租户即可获取数据

此风险已于 2026 年 8 月 16 日披露给 Databricks，但被认定属于“用户有责任确保上传的 Skill 不包含恶意内容”的范畴。鉴于恶意 Skill 在在线市场中的广泛传播，以及组织可能依赖的控制措施无法消除此风险，我们发布此报告以告知面临风险的相关方。

攻击链
Genie 被提示使用上传的 Skill 分析数据

Skill 通常通过在线市场分发，而该生态系统已知充斥着恶意 Skill。Databricks 确实有一套 Skill 治理系统，但 Genie Code 使用的 Skill 是从用户的个人工作区配置的，而非组织的受治理目录。

Genie 执行来自恶意 Skill 的代码

当 Genie 执行来自 Skill 的代码时，会由第二个代理进行检查，该代理会标记超出用户预期操作的命令，例如那些“向第三方发送数据”的命令。

介入代理批准运行该 Skill 代码，未能捕获其恶意能力。

Genie 指示用户打开完整的数据分析结果
当结果渲染时，会显示一个钓鱼模态框，并且用户的数据集被外泄

恶意 Skill 中的代码构建了一个 HTML 元素，服务于两个恶意目的。其一是渲染攻击者网站的覆盖层，以钓鱼方式骗取用户凭据。

另一个效果是，当模态框被渲染时（例如当用户查看结果时），来自受害者租户的数据被外泄。恶意 Skill 的代码利用其对受害者租户的访问权限收集敏感数据（如受害者的数据集），然后将这些数据构建到 HTML 显示内容中。当显示内容渲染时，恶意显示内容中的 JavaScript 会导致用户的浏览器发出网络请求，将数据外泄到攻击者的服务器。

虽然编码环境具有网络出口控制，可阻止与攻击者服务器的通信，但显示界面没有此类控制，可以将数据发送给攻击者。

负责任披露

此风险已于 2026 年 8 月 16 日报告给 Databricks。Databricks 团队认定：

“确保上传的 Skill 不包含恶意内容，最终是用户的责任。”

网络出口控制规定编码环境不得联系不受信任的外部方，这一点得到了遵守。它只是查询数据并用其构建了一个 iframe。

针对向用户渲染的显示内容的控制规定，显示内容不得从租户查询数据，这一点得到了遵守。它只是处理由 Skill 代码嵌入其中的数据。

因此，恶意 Skill 代码可以查询计算环境中的数据，将其构建到 iframe 中，而该 iframe 可以发起网络请求以窃取数据……

我们认为这种交互代表了 Databricks 威胁模型中的一个缺口，因为这两项在技术上得到遵守的保证，其目的正是为了防止最终发生的数据窃取结果。

关于恶意命令被护栏代理批准一事，Databricks 团队指出，

“自动允许功能并非旨在作为安全边界，而是一种防止不受信任的输入自动运行的控制措施。”

文档支持这一说法：

然而，由于‘自动批准’被记录为默认且‘推荐’的命令批准模式，我们认为用户在实践中不太可能遵守 discouraging 其与生产数据一起使用的指示。

对于 Genie Code 的 Skills 是从用户的个人工作区加载，而非从组织级受治理的 Catalog 加载这一事实，未给出任何声明。

我们正在 ChatGPT 中推出一种全新的视觉广告格式，扩展我们的衡量工具和合作伙伴关系，并开发新的方式来理解品牌适宜性。

ChatGPT 每周触达 12 亿人，是全球最大的 AI 原生消费者平台。广告帮助我们让更多人享受到 AI 带来的益处。这种广泛的触达是我们使命的核心，也是我们业务的一大优势。它让我们能够服务比仅靠订阅大得多的市场，同时为企业提供一种新方式，在人们探索想法、做出决策、发现与其目标相关的产品和服务时触达他们。

让产品和服务栩栩如生

我们全新的视觉广告格式帮助人们想象产品和服务如何融入他们的生活。通过展示产品灵感、产品使用方式或产品所带来体验的图片，人们可以发现新品牌、了解某个产品的独特之处，并决定购买什么。对广告主而言，这创造了通过图片讲述品牌故事的新机会。

初期，我们将在 ChatGPT 的图像生成过程中测试这种新广告格式。广告会被清晰标注，并与正在生成的图像保持分离。与我们其他广告格式一样，广告不会影响 ChatGPT 提供的回答。

测试将于本月晚些时候在美国启动，首批将面向一组广告主。

衡量 ChatGPT 广告的影响

我们对 ChatGPT 广告的衡量理念是同时支持企业内部和合作伙伴主导的衡量解决方案。今天，我们正在扩展衡量工具和合作伙伴生态，帮助广告主利用他们已经依赖的系统，了解 ChatGPT 广告如何为其业务做出贡献。

与 Hightouch、Tealium 和 LiveRamp 的集成，让广告主更容易将现有系统中的转化数据发送到 ChatGPT 广告。

我们现在支持网页和应用领域的领先归因合作伙伴，可与 AppsFlyer、Triple Whale、Adjust、DV Rockerbox、Northbeam、Branch、Singular、Kochava、Airbridge 和 Tenjin 等公司实现 Conversions API、报告和点击归因解决方案。我们还与全漏斗和高级衡量合作伙伴建立了合作关系，包括 Fospha、Measured 和 INCRMNTAL。

增量衡量在更全面理解广告业务影响方面发挥着重要作用。虽然我们在增量衡量方面的工作仍处于早期阶段，但我们正与 Haus、Measured 和 WorkMagic 合作，探索基于地理位置的实验，帮助广告主了解 ChatGPT 广告的因果影响。

早期合作伙伴的发现表明，不同衡量方法下均呈现出强劲表现。根据 DV Rockerbox，WeightWatchers 在 ChatGPT 广告上的归因每次获客成本比其付费搜索综合基准低 15.3%。WorkMagic 报告称，健康品牌 Dose 实现了统计显著的提升，其中 67% 的增量购买来自全新客户。而根据 Triple Whale，Portland Leather 来自 ChatGPT 广告的访客中有 93% 是新访客。

在我们的广告博客此处⁠（在新窗口中打开）阅读更多关于这些衡量工具和合作伙伴关系的内容。

在遵循我们的广告原则方面建立信任

对广告的信任还取决于对广告可能出现环境的理解。OpenAI 的广告政策和防护措施旨在保护用户、维护信任，并让品牌对其广告投放位置充满信心。我们的投放防护措施会评估某段对话是否适合投放广告，从而帮助避免广告出现在情绪脆弱、敏感或其他不适宜的语境中。

自动审核、人工监督和持续监控帮助我们识别和处理政策违规行为，并随着时间推移改进我们的防护措施。针对品牌自身政策所特有的狭窄投放要求，符合条件广告主现在可以使用否定短语（Negative Phrases）。

我们还在与 DoubleVerify（DV）和 Integral Ad Science（IAS）开展品牌适宜性评估试点，以帮助广告主更好地了解广告环境。这种方法允许独立合作伙伴在受控测试环境中评估我们的品牌安全标准如何应用，而无需访问私密用户对话。我们的目标是让广告主更透明地了解这些防护措施如何运作，同时保护对话隐私。

“随着广告扩展到 AI 原生环境，营销人员需要确信品牌安全保护是持久、一致且为大规模运营而构建的。IAS 的独立评估将评估 OpenAI 的防护措施在广泛且不断演变的各种场景中的表现，让广告主对品牌安全和适宜性有更大的透明度，同时保护真实用户对话的隐私。”

—— Integral Ad Science 首席执行官 Lidiane Jones

“ChatGPT 正在创造一个根本不同的广告环境，其中语境由对话本身而非页面或视频来定义。随着这些环境中的广告规模扩大，将广告投放到符合广告主适宜性目标的对话旁边变得至关重要。我们很高兴与 OpenAI 合作，目标是在尊重用户隐私的同时为这一动态环境带来独立测量，帮助广告主在探索这一新兴且充满前景的渠道时获得更大信心。”

Our approach to EU text provenance rules

AI 导读

OpenAI 公布应对 EU AI Act 的文本水印方案，发布在模型词选择中加入不可见统计信号的 textGrain 技术，API 客户即日起可对部分模型选择性开启水印，未来数周将在欧盟地区为 ChatGPT 和 Codex 输出添加隐形水印，检测器暂只向获批的研究者和专家机构开放。

我们在欧盟文本溯源规则上的做法

在当今技术条件下促进透明度。

加载中…

音频 1

分享

内容溯源帮助人们了解内容的来源、创建或编辑方式，以及其中是否包含与我们模型相关的信号。我们已公开提供工具，用于识别由我们模型生成的图像和音频。今天，我们分享针对欧盟《人工智能法案》的文本水印方案，以及它如何融入我们更广泛的工作。

欧盟《人工智能法案》要求生成式 AI 提供商以机器可读的方式使生成的文本可被识别。文本水印和检测仍属早期技术，存在显著局限，关于其益处和负责任使用的看法仍在发展中。我们的分阶段方案既反映了欧盟《人工智能法案》的要求，也反映了该技术的局限，并强调对文本水印能告诉人们什么、不能告诉人们什么的透明度：

从今天起，全球 API 客户将能够为部分模型选择启用文本水印。文本水印在 API 中默认保持关闭。

在未来几周内，我们将为欧盟境内符合条件的 ChatGPT 和 Codex 文本输出添加不可见水印。

我们开放文本水印检测器的申请。访问权限最初将仅限于经批准的研究人员和专家组织，他们可以帮助我们评估和改进这项技术。

以上仅适用于文本溯源——我们用于音频和图像的验证工具，包括我们的 openai.com/verify⁠ 网页工具和我们的 Content Provenance API⁠（在新窗口中打开），将继续向希望了解图像或音频文件是否由我们某个系统生成的组织公开开放。
我们的水印如何工作及表现如何

我们的文本水印技术 textGrain 会向模型的用词选择中添加一种不可见的统计信号。我们的检测器会寻找该信号，以评估一段文字是否包含 OpenAI 水印。有关 textGrain 工作原理的更多细节可在我们的技术报告⁠（在新窗口中打开）中找到，该报告将在未来几周内更新更多细节。我们还计划将该技术开源，以便他人在此基础上继续开发。

在我们的评估中，textGrain 达到或超过了我们测试过的其他方法的表现，包括用于文本的 SynthID。即便如此，理想条件下的强劲表现并不能保证在日常使用中可靠检测。

检测器可能犯两类错误：它们可能在不存在水印时报告存在水印——即假阳性——或漏掉存在的水印——即假阴性。以下评估说明了其中一些挑战：

更短或更受限的文本更难检测。在 1% 的目标假阳性率下，对于心理学等内容，我们的检测器在约 80% 的 200 token 段落中识别出水印，而在 400 token 段落中约为 95%。对于数学等用词灵活性较低的内容，检测率则大幅降低。

编辑会削弱水印。在一项针对 400 token 段落的评估中，将 10% 的词语替换为同义词使检测率从约 92% 降至 66%。替换 25% 的词语则使其降至 17%。

这些局限性促使我们决定仅向经过批准的研究人员和专家组织提供初始检测器访问权限，他们可以帮助我们评估可靠性和负责任的使用方式。

该图表展示了针对数学和心理学问题的带水印响应的结果，这些问题来自 ELI5 数据集⁠（在新窗口中打开），目标假阳性率为 1%。检测效果随文本长度增加而提升，但对于用词灵活性较低的内容（如数学），整体检测率显著更低。

编辑会大幅削弱水印信号。该图表展示了替换段落中 10% 或 25% 的词语如何影响检测。结果基于对来自 ELI5⁠（在新窗口中打开） 问题的带水印英文响应。

水印对输出质量的影响

在用于评估 Astra（我们最新的前沿模型）的各项基准测试中，我们未发现加水印与不加水印之间存在有意义的性能差异。

基准测试	无水印文本（Astra，max）	带水印文本（Astra，max）
Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index	49.57 分	49.76 分
AutomationBench	34.09%	34.86%
DeepSWE v1.1	72.80%	71.68%
Terminal-Bench 4.0	53.90%	56.06%
Terminal-Bench Science 0.1	56.90%	60.00%
BrowseComp	87.92%	87.35%
HealthBench Professional	64.27%	64.60%
GPQA Diamond	94.44%	93.94%
文本水印无法告诉你什么

文本水印只能提供关于我们的系统在段落中所起作用的有限信号。理解检测结果能得出和不能得出什么结论非常重要。

水印不能衡量人类的贡献。 它可以表明 OpenAI 系统生成或处理了段落的某部分，但无法说明其中包含多少人类判断、编辑或创造力。

水印不能确立所有权或责任。 它不能确定文本归谁所有、其使用是否合法、是否需要披露，或由谁负责。

水印不能识别用户。 它不会将个人、组织、账户、提示词或对话与文本关联起来。

水印不能验证准确性。 它不能告诉你段落是否真实、具有误导性、有害，或是否呈现于正确的语境中。

未检测到水印并不能证明是人类创作。 使用 OpenAI 工具生成的文本可能因过短、经过编辑或翻译而无法可靠检测。它也可能来自不受支持的模型、早于水印功能推出，或由其他公司的工具生成。

我们的下一步

在欧盟推出文本水印。 在未来几周内，我们将仅在欧盟面向所有套餐的符合条件的 ChatGPT 和 Codex 用户引入文本水印。我们不会在发布时将文本水印设为全球默认。这种区域性做法让我们有空间从实际使用和反馈中学习。

为 API 客户启用可选水印。 从今天起，全球的 API 客户将能够为部分模型选择启用带水印的文本输出。这让客户可以决定水印如何契合其透明度义务以及他们为用户提供的体验。我们还在与云合作伙伴合作，在未来几周内为通过其服务访问的 OpenAI 模型输出提供水印。

为研究人员和专家组织提供检测器访问权限。 经批准的研究人员和专家组织可从今天起申请。根据实践准则⁠（在新窗口中打开），访问权限最初将按个案授予，以支持文本来源的评估和改进。该工具将报告是否检测到 OpenAI 水印，而不会识别用户或披露其提示或对话。鉴于水印漏检和误报的风险，我们在发布时不会将其公开提供。

随着技术、标准和证据的发展，我们预计会重新审视这一方法的每个部分。

我们在内容来源方面的更广泛方法

没有任何单一来源技术本身足够，因此我们采用分层方法，结合开放标准、持久水印和验证工具。

我们为支持的图像输出添加 Content Credentials，符合 C2PA⁠（在新窗口中打开），在支持的图像和音频中嵌入不可见的 SynthID⁠（在新窗口中打开） 水印，并通过 openai.com/verify⁠ 和我们的 Content Provenance API⁠（在新窗口中打开） 提供图像和音频验证。这些技术相互补充：Content Credentials 可以记录文件的来源和历史，而不可见水印可以在元数据被移除时保留信号。

正如我们在选举保障工作中所述，来源信息可以帮助人们和平台评估可能具有误导性的 AI 生成内容，包括深度伪造。我们将这些信号与政策、滥用检测、报告、调查和执法相结合，并与研究人员、标准机构、平台和民间社会合作，使来源信息在更广泛的生态系统中发挥作用。

将来源信息扩展到文本需要考虑其被重写、翻译或编辑的容易程度。正如我们在六月所讨论的，我们的方法必须反映当前技术的实际局限。我们将继续改进检测，研究水印如何经受编辑和翻译，并探索更有意义地区分 AI 辅助与 AI 创作的方法。我们将随着证据、标准和监管要求的发展调整我们的方法，并在我们认为结果可以被负责任地解读时扩大检测器的访问权限。

Is there more to the MMO resurgence than just nostalgia?
Here’s The Dring: Let’s discuss the return of World of Warcraft, RuneScape and Aion
Christopher Dring
16 hours ago
∙ Paid
Good morning!
Did you watch SNL this week? No, me neither. But I’ve seen the GTA vs Zelda sketch, and (eye-rolling joke about gamers being virgins aside) I quite enjoyed it. Maybe it’s because they referred to the two games as being the industry’s “Barbenheimer moment”. Perhaps the SNL writers are readers of TGB?
Although… is it just me, or did the audience seem to prefer the idea of wandering Hyrule solving puzzles, over driving around Vice city and robbing banks?
Anyway, we have some pretty big episodes for you this week. Tomorrow, we have a big interview with a former Xbox studio. And on Thursday, we’re going to be joined by both Meta and Pearl Abyss (that’s the Crimson Desert folks). Plus, it’s been a few weeks, but we’ve got some data to share on who came out top in a busy September for video game releases.
But that’s for the week ahead. Today, I’m talking about something I really wasn’t expecting to talk about… the return of the MMORPG.
Enjoy!
Somehow, MMOs returned
I love this industry sometimes.
Just when you think the script has been written. Just when you think you know what the business is about to do. Something unexpected happens.
After months of talking about GTA 6 and Zelda and the jeopardy around consoles and who might emerge triumphant in a congested September release window… something ancient and powerful emerges that seeks to reclaim its place as one of video game’s leading genres.
Ok, hyperbole aside, it’s been a good few weeks for the MMORPG. When I joined the video game media in the mid-2000s, it felt like everyone was making one. World of Warcraft had become a mega hit and, as is often the case in entertainment, everyone thought they’d try to replicate it. The majority of those attempts didn’t work out.

2026年1-8月韩国广告支出达40亿美元创历史新高
韩国数字广告市场阶梯式强劲增长，2026年8月数字广告支出与曝光量均来到历史新高位。2026年1-8月广告支出同比增长26%，达到40亿美元；广告曝光量同比增长33%，逼近9900亿次。曝光增速明显高于预算增速，广告主在扩大投放规模的同时，持续提升触达效率。
从全年投放节奏看，韩国数字广告市场呈现清晰的季节性波动：农历新年前后步入阶段性投放低谷；3月迎来首轮预算回暖，是新品上市、春季营销、品牌推广及电商活动集中重启的核心窗口期；7–8月受暑期消费、旅游出行、电商暑期档与游戏旺季的需求释放带动，广告规模进入第二轮增长区间；Q4则在年末节日大促的驱动下持续上行，触及全年投放峰值。
消费行业稳住广告规模，服务行业贡献广告增量，AI驱动数字原生行业高速扩张
韩国数字广告市场呈全品类扩张态势，广告增长动力正从传统消费行业向服务业和数字原生行业加速延伸。购物、快消等消费行业仍是最大广告曝光来源。金融、餐饮、旅游、生活方式等服务行业广告曝光增速均超过50%，正成为新的增长引擎。
AI浪潮催生新一轮数字原生广告需求：以生成式AI、多媒体设计软件及各类实用工具为代表的软件行业广告曝光同比激增125%，AI产品正快速进入大众应用阶段，软件厂商进一步加大数字获客投入。
金融、餐饮等本土服务赛道，Kakao广告曝光占比突破30%
不同行业根据消费者决策链路的不同，选择最接近其核心消费场景和转化节点的渠道。购物、快消、媒体娱乐等多数行业中，Meta系平台曝光量占比均超过50%。
Kakao凭借对韩国消费者日常即时消费的渗透，在当地金融和餐饮服务行业中的广告曝光量占比超过30%。游戏行业对YouTube和移动应用广告的高依赖，则反映出行业“视觉化内容驱动”和移动端获客的独特模式。
从电子、漫画、汽车、游戏到美妆，韩国品牌进一步升级K-Brand全球化
韩国品牌凭借技术、内容、设计、审美等独特优势，正从电子、漫画、汽车、游戏、美妆等多个路径，加速全球化扩张。Samsung以超大规模广告曝光建立全球消费电子品牌优势；NAVER、Kakao以Webtoon等内容IP为抓手扩大海外用户触达；Netmarble、KRAFTON、Nexon、Pearl Abyss等游戏企业通过PC/主机平台加速获客；Hyundai、Kia、Hankook Tire则以区域化营销扩大海外汽车市场；Goodai Global通过多品牌组合向全球美妆平台升级。
韩泰轮胎(Hankook Tire)以33%的数字广告声量占比领跑欧洲头部汽车零部件品牌。公司签约成为UEFA (欧洲足球协会联盟)、Formula E (世界电动方程式锦标赛) 及WRC (世界拉力锦标赛) 三大顶级体育IP的官方合作伙伴，构建起足球赛事实现大众广泛触达、电动方程式夯实电动车科技背书、拉力锦标赛完成赛车性能认证的多层次体育营销矩阵，同时协同YouTube、Instagram、Facebook三大海外社交平台，实现数字化声量放大，持续夯实高端品牌定位。
中国品牌在韩国多个消费电子细分赛道建立领先的数字营销声量
从相机、扫地机器人、耳机到3D打印，中国品牌正在通过技术创新和高强度数字营销，在韩国多个消费电子细分市场建立极具规模的数字营销声量：大疆 (DJI) 以48%的广告SOV主导相机市场，石头科技 (Roborock) 以47%的SOV占据清洁赛道，韶音 (Shokz) 在耳机市场SOV达到36%，拓竹科技 (Bambu Lab) 更以81%SOV形成3D打印领域的高度集中。
